tip.cash: Money in the bank. Sales minus parts, rent and late-night development.
tip.brand: Brand (0–100). Good reviews push it up, and a strong brand sells every phone a little easier.
tip.fans: Fans pre-order at launch. Every well-reviewed phone wins a few more.
tip.date: Game time. At 1× a day takes 5 seconds.
tip.design: Design 0–10: material, thinness, screen-to-body, size, color and proportions – judged against what people expect this year.
tip.tech: Tech 0–10: chip, display, battery, camera, storage and RAM – judged against what the market expects this year.
tip.review: Where the critics will probably land (±0.5). Better reviews sell a lot more phones.
tip.unitCost: What one phone costs you: parts, plastic, assembly, box.
tip.price: Shelf price. Set to a fair value for now – you get to pick it once you have an office.
tip.margin: What you keep from each phone sold.
tip.devTime: Game days until the prototype works (you, alone, at a workbench).
tip.devCost: Parts and prototypes. Paid up front.
tip.weekly: Likely sales in the first weeks. The garage can hand-build 50 phones a week.

good.color: A palette with genuine restraint – rare at this price.

good.display: Its size feels considered, not chased.

bad.battery: Anxious about its own battery, and so are we.
bad.price: Ambitiously priced for what it is.

bad.price: price/perf ratio: poor. wait for a sale.
